title: Government borrowing in Corvel: the real interest rate, investment and the capital stock

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: The government of Corvel, an invented country, runs a large budget deficit and pays for it by borrowing. Draw a correctly labeled graph of Corvel's loanable funds market. Show the effect of the government's borrowing as a change in the demand for loanable funds, and label the new real interest rate r2.

slips.SLF: The question asks you to show the borrowing as a change in demand: the government is an extra borrower.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: Real interest rate on the vertical axis, Quantity of loanable funds on the horizontal axis, a downward-sloping demand and an upward-sloping supply of loanable funds
accept: r and Q as axis labels

rubric.point: The demand for loanable funds shifted to the right
accept: an arrow showing the rightward shift of DLF

rubric.point: A new equilibrium with a higher real interest rate, r2 above r1
accept: the higher real rate marked on the vertical axis

parts.sample: The vertical axis is the Real interest rate and the horizontal axis the Quantity of loanable funds; DLF slopes down and SLF slopes up, crossing at r1. The government's borrowing shifts DLF right to DLF2, so the real interest rate rises to r2.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain how the change in the real interest rate affects private investment in Corvel.

rubric.point: Explains that the higher real interest rate raises the cost of borrowing, so private investment falls
accept: crowding out: firms invest less at the higher real rate

parts.sample: The higher real interest rate makes borrowing more costly for firms, so they carry out fewer investment projects and private investment falls. The government's borrowing crowds out private investment.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Identify the effect of the change in private investment on the growth of Corvel's capital stock and potential output over time.

rubric.point: States that both grow more slowly (the capital stock and potential output are smaller than they would otherwise be)
accept: slower growth of the capital stock and of full-employment output

parts.sample: With less private investment, fewer machines and buildings are added each year, so Corvel's capital stock, and with it potential output, grows more slowly than it would have.
